title: Spot the Flaw: Dimensional Edition
brief: This e-commerce star was handed off for review before it ships to the BI team. It is structurally valid, but it has three dimensional-design flaws that will bite in production: a mis-typed fact name, an undeclared grain, and a fan-out trap between two facts. Find and fix all three, then re-validate until the model is clean.

entities.description: Sales transactions, one line per product sold.

columns.name: sale_id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the sale line.

entities.description: Product returns, one row per returned line.

columns.name: sale_id
columns.description: FK to the originating sale line.

expected_flaws.hint: One entity is a FACT but isn't named like one. What prefix do fact tables use?
expected_flaws.fix: Rename the entity to 'fact_sales' so its type is obvious to consumers.

expected_flaws.hint: Before adding measures, every fact needs one sentence: what does a single row mean?
expected_flaws.fix: Declare the grain, e.g. 'one row per sale line', on the sales fact.

expected_flaws.hint: Two FACT tables are joined directly. Aggregating across that join can double-count.
expected_flaws.fix: Don't relate fact-to-fact. Relate both facts to a conformed dimension (e.g. dim_date / dim_product), and analyze returns at their own grain.

solution_notes: The clean model renames 'sales' to 'fact_sales' with grain 'one row per sale line', keeps fact_returns at its own grain, and removes the fact_returns -> sales relationship (returns and sales conform through shared dimensions rather than a direct fact-to-fact join). After the fixes, re-validation shows no NAMING_CONVENTION, MISSING_GRAIN, or FAN_OUT_RISK issues.
